subject: Private Offer: modular packaging vs committed seats + reseller earnout
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@blueridge.com>, procurement@blueridge.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private Offer: modular packaging vs committed seats + reseller earnout

Aaron / team —

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. Per our follow-up, I wanted to put the options on the table so procurement can feed this into your internal evaluation:

1) Committed Capacity (3-yr) — Reserved node-hours with a blended unit price (list price discount + capacity credit). Predictable for you, allows us to give the deepest list-price reduction.
2) Modular / Metered Packaging — Lower up-front commit, usage-based billing with tiered volume discounts and optional add-ons (replica nodes, premium support). Better for workload variability but list-price discount is smaller.

Two asks from our side as we draft the private offer:
- Can you confirm the internal reseller path? You mentioned a preferred systems integrator that will resell the product in-country; we need the target reseller margin so we can model net economics (examples below).
- Which packaging does procurement prefer from a PO + budget perspective (commit vs modular)? If you need, I can sketch a hybrid: a small committed core + modular overage tiers.

Initial modeling note: at 12% reseller margin we can offer ~18% off list for a 3-yr commit at the volume band you described; at 16% reseller margin the net-to-BlueRidge goes down materially and our list discount compresses to ~12%. I attached a short SOW and a pricing workbook with scenario tabs.

Attachments: BR_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW), pricing-scenarios.xlsx (workbook)

Next steps: if procurement can confirm reseller margin target and preferred packaging by EOD Tuesday 9/29, we will produce a private-offer draft and a one-page economics memo for finance.

Thanks —
David
David Kim
Sr. Sales Manager, Marketplace & Channel
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: BR_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF) - 1.2MB]
[Attachment: pricing-scenarios.xlsx (Excel) - 90KB]

From: Aaron Li <aaron.li@blueridge.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@blueridge.com
Date: 2026-09-25T13:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: modular packaging vs committed seats + reseller earnout

David —

Appreciate the clear options. A few quick clarifications from procurement / finance here at BlueRidge:

- Reseller: we intend to route through NovaSys (our systems integrator partner). Their commercial expectation is a 15% margin on software resale (standard for their bundled services).
- Packaging preference: Finance leans toward a hybrid approach — a 12-month minimum core commit that locks a base price + metered overage beyond that. Procurement wants the option to renew/scale at fixed bands (0-50k, 50-200k, 200k+ node-hours).

Two asks back to you:
1) Can you show a 12-month hybrid vs 36-month pure commit comparison (total contracted value + expected first-year cashflow)?
2) If NovaSys must receive 15% reseller margin, how does that change the list discount you can offer BlueRidge?

We reviewed the SOW and the workbook quickly — docs look fine but we may have a few legal redlines later.

— Aaron
Aaron Li | Head of Procurement, BlueRidge Systems
aaron.li@blueridge.com
[Note: procurement@blueridge.com is looped for routing]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@blueridge.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: modular packaging vs committed seats + reseller earnout

Aaron —

Thanks for confirming NovaSys and the 15% target. I've pulled a quick sensitivity into the pricing workbook (tab: reseller_impact). High level:

- 36-month commit: gross list discount to BlueRidge can be 20% if reseller margin is 12%; with 15% reseller the deepest we can go while maintaining our margin guardrails is ~14% off list.
- 12-month hybrid (core + metered overage): we can preserve near-term cashflow by front-loading 40% of the first-year TCV into the core commit. That gets BlueRidge closer to the 36-month net in year 1 while keeping renewal optional.

A recommended commercial structure to keep NovaSys whole and protect your P&L:
- Offer a 12-month core commit at a slightly higher unit price than a 36-month list-discount (gives you budget predictability).
- Include a reseller uplift clause: NovaSys receives 15% of list on any resale; Redwood will compute net-of-reseller list discount in the private-offer so BlueRidge invoices are clean.
- Add a 90-day renewal window with a renewal SKU that steps down pricing if you convert to a 36-month commit in the renewal window.

If that sounds acceptable I can prepare two private-offer drafts: 1) 12-month hybrid with NovaSys 15% carveout, 2) 36-month commit with tiered discount. Which would you like first?

I can also add a short paragraph in the offer about invoicing flow (BlueRidge pays NovaSys; NovaSys remits to Redwood under reseller agreement) if procurement needs it for the PO.

Cheers,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Private Offers & Marketplace
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@blueridge.com>, procurement@blueridge.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: modular packaging vs committed seats + reseller earnout

Aaron / team —

Thanks — this is helpful. Delivering on Irene's note, we'll do the two drafts but prioritize the 12-month hybrid (per your finance preference) so you can get the PO approved faster. Deliverable timeline:
- Monday 9/30 by EOD PT: 12-month hybrid private-offer (PDF) + one-pager economics with cashflow table and NovaSys 15% impact shown.
- Wednesday 10/02: 36-month commit private-offer + negotiation markups ready.

One operational note for procurement: please confirm the billing party for the PO (BlueRidge -> NovaSys -> Redwood vs BlueRidge -> Redwood with NovaSys invoice). We will put the reseller carveout language in either arrangement, but the invoicing path changes the payment flow we model in finance.

I'll attach the draft economics memo once it's built (pricing-scenarios.xlsx updated). If procurement can confirm billing path and whether they want the renewal SKU at the time of the first draft, that will speed review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
David
[Attachment: pricing-scenarios.xlsx (updated) - 95KB]
